analysis.title: GS US TMT .. stocks ..
key_insights: Nasdaq 100 rose about 250 bps on the day and is back above its 200-day moving average and above pre-Election levels. The VIX is at a 17 handle as index volatility resets lower. The desk attributes the move to cleaner positioning, lower vol and Election narratives being digested or put on the back burner.
The SOX is approaching its own 200-day moving average.

The desk sees relatively little consensus in the market. Debate centers on where the AI/semis cycle stands, what is priced in, and whether this is a bear market bounce or a bull market forming. Positive sentiment on the Hyperscalers may be the exception.

Software dispersion has picked up, including within the Cyber and Data Infra cohorts. Internet has become squeezy and difficult to trade. The desk calls positioning and sentiment a 'blank slate' going into 2027.
Top client inbounds: why Tech/AI is bouncing so hard, SNDK up 16%, lag in ABNB and in cloud service providers, earnings set-ups (CSCO, AMAT, DIS), and squeezes in DUOL, RDDT and SNAP types.

Semis are about 25% off YTD highs and nearly 20% above the local lows, with limited participation from NVDA. AMD is up 40% in 4 days. Clients debate rotating into high-beta, high gross margin names versus staying in higher quality names on the view that AI volatility persists.

DASH and gig economy inbounds have picked up as DASH de-rated to cycle lows of about 15x forward EBITDA. Debates cover competition (Uber Eats and Amazon tie-up), organic versus inorganic growth (the CART acquisition, following the Deliveroo acquisition last year), and agentic workflows entering an already low-friction ordering experience.

LYV is up about 26% YTD. At yesterday's analyst day, management raised the Venue Nation AOI opportunity to $925M from $750M, driven by adding 38 large venues through 2031 at 20%+ IRRs (versus 48 venues by 2031 previously). The total is $725M from pipeline venues plus venues opened in 2025-2026 and $200M from enhancements to existing venues. The desk is starting conversations about an encore into 2027.

NVDA closed yesterday with a 14-day RSI of about 24, the lowest since mid-2019. The two highest-volume days of the past year came Monday and Tuesday this week, and NVDA shed about $430bn of market cap. It lagged semis by about 17 points over 3 days, the largest 3-day spread this decade. Investor debate is emerging ahead of NVDA earnings next week.

Memory (MU, SNDK, HDDs): bulls cite 2-4x forward P/E near tangible book value, new capital return programs (all eyes on MU earnings), firm or rising spot prices (especially DRAM) and guided favorable supply/demand through 2027+. Bears worry about over-earning from ASP tailwinds early in the cycle, unresolved supply from new entrants, and low P/E multiples in cycles being as much a bear case as a bull case.

TTWO is up 7 of the last 8 sessions, about 20% over the stretch, and is not seen as crowded. Bulls cite a cheap stock ahead of the GTA 6 cycle, beat/raise potential, and mobile self-help with improving advertising and D2C growth. Bears cite F2Q net bookings and RCS light due to NBA 2K27, GTA launch/discovery nuances, Mobile volatility (Color Block Jam) and AI tooling uncertainty.

DDOG and DT are each down over 30% in the last ~2 weeks after mixed results, creating debate over acceleration visibility. A GIR meeting with Dynatrace's Head of IR gave visibility into the F2H setup. The full-year outlook does not require every slipped opportunity to close.
